title: Bill Donovan:
title_short: Bill Donovan · Kids who wouldn't mix
headline: An after-school program supervisor says Math Hoops brings sports kids and math kids to the same table, and they learn without noticing.
story: Bill runs the after-school program at Maspeth Town Hall. Sports kids come for the NBA, math kids come for the math, and kids who would never talk to each other end up at the same table.
He saw one student pick the game up fast and start coaching the others. His message is the one educators need: you can combine learning with sports, and the kids don't even realize they're learning.

Loops: L1 “How do they not notice?” opens at 0:00 and closes at the button. L2 “What changed in the room?” opens at 0:08 and closes at 0:28. Stakes: kids who ordinarily wouldn't be interacting with one another.

transcript:
--- 20261012_C5299.MP4 ---
[00:00.0] All right, so first question I have for you here,
[00:03.0] can you introduce yourself, say and spell your name for me
[00:06.3] and tell me your job title also?
[00:08.4] Sure thing.
[00:09.3] My name is Bill Donovan, that's spelled D-O-N-O-V-A-N.
[00:14.9] I'm a program supervisor at MassFit Town Hall.
[00:18.0] My main responsibility is bringing in vendors
[00:20.4] and subcontractors to provide curriculum to our children.
[00:24.3] Awesome, thank you, Bill.
[00:25.7] So first question I have for you is,
[00:28.0] what was your first reaction
[00:29.7] when you learned about this program here?
[00:32.4] So when we first learned about MBA Math Hoops,
[00:35.9] we'd already had some exposure to LearnFresh
[00:38.5] from Mets Math Pits a couple of years ago
[00:41.5] that was extremely well received by our participants
[00:44.9] as well as our staff members.
[00:46.5] So we were very excited when we had the opportunity
[00:48.9] to work with LearnFresh again.
[00:51.3] Awesome, and walk me through what Math Hoops looks like
[00:55.4] in your classroom.
[00:57.3] So the reason we enjoy MBA Math Hoops,
[01:01.3] we have a lot of programs that we're doing sports.
[01:05.1] We have other STEM and STEAM activities.
[01:08.0] This is one of the few where we can combine the two.
[01:11.1] So we have the sports kids who are into it because it's MBA,
[01:14.7] and then we have the STEM, the more,
[01:16.8] I don't wanna say they're academically inclined
[01:19.2] participants, but the students who are more
[01:20.9] into the math aspect of it.
[01:22.7] So we've seen a nice cross,
[01:25.1] I guess a cross-pollination of children
[01:27.6] who ordinarily wouldn't be interacting with one another
[01:31.1] the way they do on a daily basis.
[01:33.3] Very cool.
[01:34.4] So what did you notice in your students
[01:38.3] after playing Math Hoops?
[01:40.4] Well, what I noticed with the students was some of them
[01:43.1] who really weren't into the basketball so much
[01:47.1] started talking about different players and names
[01:50.6] and different concepts and wanting to watch basketball
[01:54.6] and on the flip side, some of the kids who are really
[01:58.1] into basketball are starting to understand
[02:00.8] the statistical importance of things that they see
[02:03.6] when they're watching games.
[02:05.6] Awesome.
[02:06.5] So was there a student whose experience or learning
[02:10.5] in the Math Hoops program caught you off guard?
[02:13.9] I'm sorry, I couldn't hear that.
[02:15.4] Oh yeah, you're good.
[02:16.3] The kids are so excited.
[02:17.2] Hey, no worries.
[02:18.2] Was there a student whose experience or learning
[02:21.8] while playing Math Hoops caught you off guard
[02:24.4] that you can remember?
[02:26.1] No one really caught me off guard,
[02:28.0] but what I did see with one student in particular,
[02:30.9] which was a nice outcome of this,
[02:33.3] is that he understood the game a little better than others
[02:37.0] and picked up on it pretty quickly
[02:39.1] to the point where he's now helping coach
[02:42.0] some of the kids who don't know the game as well.
[02:44.4] So we thought this was, hey, this is great.
[02:46.5] It's sports, it's academics, it's STEM, it's math,
[02:50.4] but we also have at least one student, if not more,
[02:53.6] who we saw develop some leadership skills
[02:56.6] based on the program.
[02:57.9] Oh wow, very cool.
[02:59.5] So what do you hope for the future
[03:02.4] of Math Hoops in your class?
[03:04.9] So today's event, I think, has taken
[03:08.9] what we were doing in the classroom to the next level.
[03:12.0] So hopefully the 27 students we have here from IS73,
[03:17.5] they continue playing the game
[03:19.4] during our regular program hours,
[03:21.4] and maybe when some of their friends
[03:23.0] see them wearing a NBA Math Hoops shirt,
[03:26.0] they'll be intrigued by the possibility
[03:28.2] and we'll have even more kids playing on a day-to-day basis.
[03:31.7] Yeah, totally, I know I would have been when I was a kid.
[03:34.0] So last couple questions I have for you, are you happy?
[03:38.2] Am I happy?
[03:39.4] I'm extremely happy right now.
[03:41.3] A couple of days ago, because today is a holiday,
[03:44.2] we weren't sure we were gonna have the turnout
[03:46.4] that we had today, and you can hear in the background
[03:50.0] the kids laughing and having fun with one another.
[03:52.2] So I'm very happy.
[03:54.4] Amazing, and if you had one message to share
[03:56.7] with whoever might watch this, what would you wanna say?
[03:59.8] That it is possible to combine learning with sports,
[04:06.1] and sometimes when you do things and the kids are having fun,
[04:10.1] they don't even realize they're learning,
[04:11.5] and sometimes that makes for the best kind of learning.
[04:14.9] Amazing, anything else you wanna share?
[04:16.7] No, just today was a great day,
[04:19.1] and we have a couple hours left,
[04:20.6] so I'm sure the remainder will be equally as great
[04:23.8] as it's been so far.
[04:25.1] Absolutely, perfect, that's all I got for you right there.
